rationale: REPLACE_WITH_OWNER_RATIONALE -- this record supersedes decisions/owner-approvals/control-gate-pin-bump-launch-a-draft.json (v1), which is kept in place only as a frozen record of the discovered structural impossibility, not as a candidate for signature. v1 requires the signed record to state the exact commit SHA (candidateTree) of the commit that will contain it; that commit's tree necessarily changes when the record is added to product/dependency-verification.json, so it changes its own resulting SHA -- a commit cannot state its own hash inside itself. This v2 schema (scripts/verify-control-dependencies.mjs: CONTROL_PIN_BUMP_SCHEMA_V2, baseCheckerPinBumpErrorsV2) drops baseTree/candidateTree entirely and binds only deterministic content that is fully known before the record is authored: the exact bytes of product/dependency-pins.json (basePinsSha256/candidatePinsSha256), the exact base checker blob this approval was reviewed against (baseChecker), and the exact enumerated control-surface digest changes (controls) via the existing sameControlChanges comparison -- unchanged from v1. Positive/negative tests proving this in scripts/tests/control-dependencies.test.mjs: 'the base control checker permits a v2 owner-approved pin bump with no commit-SHA binding', 'a v2 pin bump approval does not depend on the commit-SHA that ships it' (same approval object checked against two different candidateTree values, both pass), 'rejects a v2 pin bump whose approval token is not a formal owner token', 'rejects a v2 pin bump record carrying a v1-only field' (exact-keys check via sameKeys/CONTROL_PIN_BUMP_V2_KEYS), and 'rejects a v2 pin bump approved for one control-surface change but shipped with another' (an unrelated pinned control file mutated after the approval was computed is refused, proving an unchanged approval cannot admit altered controls it never enumerated). The controls entries below are the complete actual control-surface digest delta between protected base 37c0f955f76410e9c9863e77cdc33fd48ffd1306 and candidate 157852aabcf13d31e5ecad2bd2353358d3fb7eaf: four protected CI workflows, the Robinhood archive-fork integration test, and this verifier. product/dependency-pins.json was corrected this turn (its controlDependencyVerifier pin was stale, still declaring the pre-v2 checker digest -- a bookkeeping bug in a prior turn, not a security-relevant control change; fixed so the pin file is internally consistent with the actual tracked checker bytes, per Terra's A5 finding), so candidatePinsSha256 below reflects the corrected file, not the earlier, wrong value.

bootstrapIntervention.problem: This is a PROVEN impossibility for the ordinary required-check path, not an inconvenience -- confirmed by reading .github/workflows/control-gate.yml:43-62 (pull-request job) and its push-job twin: the workflow extracts scripts/verify-control-dependencies.mjs and scripts/lib/util.mjs FROM THE PROTECTED BASE COMMIT ONLY (`git show "${range_base}:scripts/verify-control-dependencies.mjs" > ...; node "${base_control_root}/..." --base-control "$range_base" "$range_head"`), then runs that extracted base script against the candidate's data. It never executes any checker code from the candidate. As long as the protected base (canonical main) does not yet contain this v2 dispatch code, the ONLY validation logic that ever actually runs is the old v1-only baseCheckerPinBumpErrors -- which does not recognize schema hookemon.control-gate-pin-bump.v2 at all and would evaluate any v2 record's baseTree/candidateTree fields as absent/undefined, failing the v1 equality check. So no candidate commit, however it is authored, can ever cause the REQUIRED GitHub control-gate/v4-gates checks to report PASSED for a v2 record, until v2-aware code already exists on the protected base -- and it cannot reach the protected base through an ordinary PR without first passing that exact check. This is a genuine bootstrap deadlock internal to the current architecture, not something any record content, schema design, or in-repo mechanism can route around.
bootstrapIntervention.provenBySource: Confirmed by direct inspection of .github/workflows/control-gate.yml (both the pull_request_target 'pull-request' job and the push job use `git show <base>:scripts/verify-control-dependencies.mjs` to build the executed script, never the candidate's copy) and independently corroborated by Terra's A5 review (A5-terra-verification.md): 'There remains no path to put v2 support into a base that only recognizes v1 without an external root-of-trust decision.'
bootstrapIntervention.ineffectiveOptionRuledOut: A previously recommended using the existing `node scripts/v4.mjs gate override <phase> ...` command as the bootstrap action. Terra's A5 review proved this does not work: that command only writes a project-internal phase-gate receipt (scripts/lib/gates.mjs) inside this repo's own v4 ledger; GitHub's REQUIRED control-gate/v4-gates checks are independent CI jobs that never read that receipt. Running `gate override` cannot turn the required GitHub check green and is not a bootstrap action at all -- withdrawn, not recommended below.
bootstrapIntervention.exactConstraintTheOwnerWouldNeedToChange: There is no available action -- for A, for an operator, or for the owner -- that simultaneously satisfies all three of: (1) the ordinary required GitHub control-gate/v4-gates checks report a genuine PASSED result for the commit that first introduces v2-aware code, (2) no ruleset/branch-protection bypass or admin override of that specific required check is used, and (3) no fabricated/self-approved token is written. (1) is impossible without the base already trusting v2, which by definition it does not yet. The owner's own stated policy requires (2) and (3) unconditionally. Making the v2 migration reachable at all therefore requires the owner to consciously accept exactly one, explicit, logged exception to (2) -- an admin action that admits this single, specific, pre-reviewed bootstrap commit onto the protected base outside the ordinary required-check gate (for example: a repository-admin merge that is permitted to bypass required status checks for this one commit, used exactly once, with the exact reviewed diff and this record as the citation) -- or to decide the v2 migration is not worth that exception and leave the control gate on its current, structurally-limited v1 protocol. A is not recommending which of these the owner should choose; A is stating that no third option exists.
bootstrapIntervention.afterBootstrap: Once a single commit containing working v2-schema-aware code is admitted onto the protected base by whichever route the owner chooses, all LATER control-surface pin bumps can use ordinary v2 records through the normal required-check path with no further exception, because at that point the checker enforcing v2 is itself already part of the trusted base tree that future candidates are compared against.
